81333.subject: Changelog #0313: October 21 security incident
81333.body:
This week's changelog: our response to the October 21 incident and recommended actions.

Changelog

This week, we've been responding to the October 21 security incident, restoring systems, and helping customers secure their credentials. We’re deeply sorry for the disruption and the additional burden this has placed on you.

The incident involved unauthorized access to Railway's internal systems. We've taken steps to contain it and restore affected services, and we're investigating the impact with external incident response experts.

As a precaution, we recommend the following:

- Revoke and replace sensitive credentials stored on Railway before October 21.
- Remove public network access to databases.
- Review GitHub audit logs and installed app access.
- Check container registry audit logs for unexpected activity.

Our preliminary incident report explains what happened, the impact, and our response. The investigation is ongoing, and we'll share a follow-up when it concludes.

Read the incident report: https://blog.railway.com/p/preliminary-report-october-security-incident

If you have questions or need help, contact support@railway.com.

- The Railway team

Unsubscribe: https://railway.com/preferences?token=4c2e4edf-bffd-4b7a-ad7d-a802198020ea

# Friday charts: Cash is king again — but for a new reason

It’s been a record-breaking year in US capital markets: To name just a few, we’ve had the largest-ever IPO (SpaceX), capital raises (Google and SK Hynix), private-equity round (OpenAI), private-credit deal (Broadcom), and public bond issue (Amazon).

The Economist [calls](https://www.economist.com/business/2026/09/30/the-era-of-speedball-capitalism-has-dawned) it “speedball capitalism”: Things that would have been the defining event of any other year warrant barely a day’s attention in 2026.

That is not, however, because investors have watched too many TikToks and can no longer focus. Instead, investing has sped up because there are so, so many things to invest in: rockets, data centers, power plants, robots, self-driving cars — all of a sudden, we’re overrun with opportunities to invest in real, tangible things. 

Like war dogs.

This morning, a group of prominent venture capital firms announced a $200 million investment in [Warhound](https://warhound.com), a startup that will genetically engineer dogs to serve in the US military, law enforcement, and first responders.

A co-founder [told](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/22/ben-lamm-raises-200m-for-warhound-to-engineer-war-dogs-and-arm-them-with-anduril-gear/) Tech Crunch the dogs could be enhanced for health, longevity, speed, agility, and sense of smell.
